name: qualify-async-fanout-go
note: Expected: good, good-pool, and good-ctx pass (good-ctx changes the gateway client's signatures, so the fixture_tests measure fails while existing_commands_unchanged passes); sequential fails within_budget only (it finishes well before the hard limit, so its report is judged and right); unbounded and numcpu (one read per CPU, more than 16 wherever the run is valid) fail within_limit and the two report checks (connections past 16 are dropped); no-timeout fails within_budget, failures_handled (ERR 504 after 30 s instead of no answer), and no_held_connections; abandoned and abandoned-cap12 fail within_limit and the report checks (abandoned connections pile up past 16 whatever the client's own cap) but exit on time; paced fails within_limit and the report checks (no bound on open connections); pool-holds fails no_held_connections (its 16 workers stay on silent inverters' connections for the gateway's 30 s in the outage; it never goes over the limit, and within_budget depends on whether the outage's time limit falls below its 35 s); overall-deadline fails answered_inverters_correct, failures_handled, and no_held_connections; long-timeout fails failures_handled and no_held_connections (late inverters printed as readings, silent ones' connections held 10 s); closewrite fails every check but builds (the gateway takes its half-close as hanging up, as docs/gateway.md says; its own tests fail too); leaks fails no_work_after_exit only; wrong fails failures_handled only; noop fails everything but builds and existing_commands_unchanged. Command arms need no toolchain: the check builds and runs everything with the host's Go. The run is invalid on a host where the check sees 16 CPUs or fewer.
